newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Feb 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Feb 10.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company -- CLARKE SHUNS CALLS FOR RATE RISE

Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke has overruled pressure from Treasury officials and the Bank of England to raise interest rates. The latest monthly report from the Bank, due this week, is expected to show that inflation is likely to overshoot the two-year rolling target on the basis of current interest rates. A Treasury official is reported as saying that "it has been clear for some time that it is the timing of the general election which is driving him (the chancellor)".
-- G7 RESOLVES TO PUT BRAKES ON RISING DOLLAR

Finance ministers and central bank governors of the Group of Seven leading industrialised nations have issued a statement claiming they believed "major misalignments" apparent on foreign exchange markets for the past two years "have to be corrected".

The comments, which follow a meeting in Berlin, leave the world's foreign exchange markets braced for tense trading conditions on Monday. The move will seek to curtail the recent rise of the U.S. dollar.
-- GKN FACES ESCALATION OF CLAIM TO $740 MILLION

Lawyers acting for franchise operators Meineke Discount Mufflers, the U.S. specialist exhaust retailer of UK group GKN, are expected this week to escalate the lawsuit currently filed against GKN. The lawyers are expected to file for more than $740 million following a court decision in December in which a North Carolina jury awarded $347 million against GKN for allegedly defrauding the franchise operators. The case is one of the largest U.S. commercial damages lawsuits brought against a UK company.
-- INVESTMENT BANKS CALL IN SNOOPS TO STEM DEFECTIONS

Some investment banks in the City of London are reported to be hiring private investigators to spy on employees they suspect may be about to leave. As competition intensifies among the banks for teams of traders, a small number of them have called in agencies to tape telephone conversations, including one which took place in a public house. The revelations follow the highly publicised case of Nicola Horlick, who was suspended by Morgan Grenfell Asset Management for allegedly planning a mass defection of staff to rivals ABN Amro.
-- SONY EXECUTIVE ATTACKS 'INSULAR' HOLLYWOOD

A senior executive at Japanese media and entertainment group Sony Corp has launched an attack on the insular and complacent attitudes of the U.S. film and television production industry. Jeff Sagansky, the newly-installed president of Sony Pictures Entertainment, claims that the U.S. industry is losing ground in Europe and risks missing opportunities in Asia and Latin America. He warned that Hollywood must shed its self-congratulatory and short-term views and invest more in foreign production.
-- CENTRICA FACES BLOCK ON USING BRITISH GAS DATABASE

The planned demerger of British Gas into the domestic gas business Centrica and BG is set to create a major headache for Centrica. The new company will face big legal obstacles to its plans to use the new centralised database which has cost it more than 100 million stg over the past two years. The list of customers, one of the biggest in Europe, will remain the property of British Gas, and Centrica faces serious data protection hurdles over its plans to use the database to market a range of products, including financial services and electricity, to its 19 million customers.
-- LLOYD'S CONSIDERS WAYS TO LIMIT GROWTH IN CAPACITY

Insurance market Lloyd's of London is reported to be considering controversial changes which could limit growth in the capacity of business it writes. In the past, some of the market's rules have encouraged the creation of excess capacity, and critics have claimed this played a role in the billions of pounds of losses suffered between 1988 and 1992. A decision will be made in the next few months over how much control the market's ruling council should have over capacity, if any.
-- BUSINESSES CONFIDENT SALES WILL INCREASE

The latest quarterly survey from business information group Dunn and Bradstreet has revealed that businesses are more confident of higher sales and profits than at any time in the past two years. The survey, which canvassed 1,600 managing directors, found that the construction sector is leading the upturn, with about 70 per cent of building firms expecting increased sales and profits.
-- CLYDE MEETS INVESTORS IN GULF BATTLE

UK oil independent Clyde Petroleum, which is fighting a 494 million stg hostile takeover bid from Gulf Canada Resources, is set to meet institutional investors on Monday in an effort to secure support for their defence. Roy Franklin, managing director of Clyde, says he hopes to persuade fund managers to support the defence on the basis of its track record and long-term prospects. Gulf Canada has eight days to win control of Clyde.
-- GAZ DE FRANCE MAY TAKE SUPPLIES FROM UK

French state-owned gas company Gaz de France may take up to three billion cubic metres of gas a year from the UK once a 500 million stg interconnector linking the UK and Europe comes onstream. In an interview with the Financial Times, Pierre Gadonneix, president of Gaz de France, said that the company may reach a deal before the end of this year on its first purchases of British Gas.
